reference.title: kitControl-LoopPoint
reference.shortdesc: This component implements a simple PID control loop. Loop objects provide closed-loop PID control (proportional, integral, derivative) at the station level. Independent gain constants configure the loop as P-only, PI, or PID.

section.p: LoopPoint is available in the HVAC folder of the kitControl palette.

propdesc.p: Selects units and configures how the value displays:
unit defines the unit of measure from acceleration to volumetric flow.
precision defines the number of decimal places.
min defines the lowest value allowed.
max defines the highest value allowed.
These facets apply to the Out value.

property.propdesc: Displays the output value for the loop.

property.propvalue: true (default) or false and null definition
property.propdesc:
Turns the loop on and off.
true enables the PID loop algorithm to execute at the rate selected by the Execute Time property.
false forces the PID loop output to a value that is dependent on the selection in the Disable Action property.
When null is checked, the value displayed defaults to the incoming value from the device.If you remove the check mark you can configure the In value.

propdesc.p: Selects units and configures how the value displays:
unit defines the unit of measure from acceleration to volumetric flow.
precision defines the number of decimal places.
min defines the lowest value allowed.
max defines the highest value allowed.
These facets apply to the input.

property.propdesc:
Defines the input value for the controlled property (for example, space temperature). This input must be valid for this object to function.
When null is checked, the value displayed defaults to the incoming value from the device.If you remove the check mark you can configure the In value.

property.propvalue: number of degrees of temperature and null definition
property.propdesc:
Defines the input value for the setpoint (for example, the space temperature setpoint). This value must be valid for this object to function. The object does not provide an integral command function for the setpoint value when entered on the property sheet.
If a commandable setpoint is required, link from a NumericWritable control point to the setpoint slot.
Controls the execution frequency for the PID algorithm.
Reports the milliseconds since the previous execution. Changing the Execute Time changes this time.

Determines if the control algorithm is direct or reverse acting.
Direct increases the loop output as the value of the controlled variable increases to greater than the setpoint value. In a temperature loop, this is considered to be a cooling application.
Reverse increases the loop output as the value of the controlled variable decreases to less than the setpoint value. In a temperature loop, this is considered to be a heating application.

Selects the value for the loop output (Out) when Loop Enable is false.
Max Value sets the loop output value to the value configured for Max Output.
Min Value sets the loop output value to the value configured for Min Output.
Hold maintains the loop output value at the last calculated value.
Zero sets the loop output value to zero (0.00).

propdesc.p: Selects units and configures how the value displays:
unit defines the unit of measure from acceleration to volumetric flow.
precision defines the number of decimal places.
min defines the lowest value allowed.
max defines the highest value allowed.
These facets apply to the tuning properties, such as the constants, Bias, and output properties.

property.propvalue: number of seconds to three decimal places
property.propdesc: Defines a value used by the loop algorithm to set the overall gain for the loop. A starting point for this value equals: output range/throttling range.
Defines the integral gain in repeats per minute. The loop algorithm uses this value (also called the reset rate) to act on the magnitude of the setpoint error. A typical starting point is 0.5.
Defines the derivative gain used by the loop algorithm to act on the rate of change of the setpoint error.
Defines an amount of output the algorithm adds to correct any offset error. The algorithm uses this value normally only with proportional control.
Defines the maximum output value that the loop algorithm can produce.
Defines the minimum output value that the loop algorithm can produce.

Defines the minimum time that the output can ramp completely from Minimum Output to Maximum Output, effectively establishing a rate-of-change slope. This component enforces this value at station startup or whenever the LoopPoint transitions from disabled to enabled.
Once Ramp Time expires, it no longer affects the output. This property is intended to prevent the loop from opening a valve or other controlled device to its maximum limit (“slamming”) during startup.The default Ramp Time is 0:00:00, or disabled. To constrain the loop output rate of change when the loop starts or is enabled, enter a reasonable Ramp Time value.

section.title: Action
section.p: ResetIntegral clears the current integral component of the loop’s output calculation. If needed, you can link this slot to another object to provide a quick purge of the integral effect. Typically, the latter would provide more of a debug utility, and should not be necessary if the LoopPoint’s configuration properties are correctly defined.
